question: What can be measured and decoded beyond scalp EEG?
metric_units: balanced accuracy, class recall, chance levels and shares are proportions in [0,1]; R² is unitless; RMSE and MAE are in m/s; sampling rates in Hz, windows and lags in seconds or milliseconds as named; counts of people, animals, trials, rows, recordings, channels, values, runs and frames are whole numbers
scope: Locally executed analyses and prepared sources beyond scalp EEG, each its own species, modality and measured quantity: human fNIRS classification of executed movements, macaque intracortical decoding of finger velocity, a numerical coverage check of human fNIRS recordings, and two sources prepared but not scored (human intracortical handwriting, human functional ultrasound). They share no metric and no ranking, none is compared with scalp EEG, and nothing joins the eight-protocol matrix. Every figure is this site's own experiment, not a score reported in a paper.

bak-fnirs-loso.title: Human fNIRS: executed finger and foot tapping, a held-out person
bak-fnirs-loso.question: Can a fixed hemodynamic classifier trained on other people tell which movement a held-out person made?
bak-fnirs-loso.label: Locally executed experiment · offline · leave one whole person out
bak-fnirs-loso.evidence: a locally executed experiment, not a score reported in a paper
bak-fnirs-loso.measured_quantity: the supplied oxy- and deoxyhemoglobin series, in mM·cm as delivered, not absolute concentrations

task.kind: executed movement, cued; not motor imagery

design.split: leave one person out: each fold fits on the other people and predicts every trial of the held-out person; every person is held out once

signal.channel_note: twenty oxy- and twenty deoxyhemoglobin series; the supplied files carry no probe coordinates
signal.processing: each window's channel mean minus the one-second pre-onset mean; no filtering applied beyond the supplied series, whose upstream preprocessing may use future samples

models.shrinkage_lda: standardization and shrinkage LDA (lsqr solver, automatic shrinkage, empirical training priors) fitted on the training people only; no channel, feature or hyperparameter search
models.source_prior: the most frequent class among the training trials, ties broken by the fixed class order; with balanced classes it predicts right-hand tapping every time

primary_metric.name: Participant-macro balanced accuracy
primary_metric.definition: each held-out person's balanced accuracy (the mean of the three class recalls), averaged over the people with equal weight

bak-fnirs-loso.class_recall_note: the recall of each class over all held-out predictions, every person together (the same number of trials in each class); a secondary point estimate without an interval

uncertainty.kind: descriptive 95% percentile interval: the fixed participant scores resampled with replacement, 2,000 draws
uncertainty.scope: It describes variation between people given the fitted folds. The folds share training people, so it is not a refit bootstrap and not an independent clinical confidence interval.
uncertainty.comparator: The training prior has no interval: every person gets the same score.

bak-fnirs-loso.reading: For a held-out person, the fixed classifier separated right-hand, left-hand and foot tapping well above the training prior, and its descriptive interval lies wholly above chance. This is offline classification of supplied hemodynamic series over a 15-second window after each task onset.
limitations: Offline, from the supplied hemodynamic series with a 15-second observation window; the upstream preprocessing may use future samples. Neither online control nor device response time is shown.
Executed movement, not motor imagery; no clinical or device-effectiveness claim.

One supplied cohort of 30 people. Task-correlated systemic or motion effects are not excluded, so the result establishes neither a brain-only signal nor cortical localization; the supplied files carry no probe coordinates.
The interval resamples fixed participant scores from overlapping leave-one-out training sets: not a refit bootstrap, not an independent clinical confidence interval.
The protocol is this site's own; it does not reproduce the authors' within-person scores.
claims_not_supported: no online or real-time control claim
no cortical localization or brain-versus-systemic-signal claim
not a reproduction of the authors' scores

independent_audit.checked: every input file hash, the marker-to-label order, whole-person folds, training-only scaling, the comparator's tie rule and prediction alignment; the confusion tables, class recalls, primary mean and bootstrap recomputed without the frozen scoring code
independent_audit.not_checked: the features were not regenerated from the raw channels and the classifier was not refit

nlb-mc-rtt-velocity.title: Macaque intracortical spiking: finger velocity within one session
nlb-mc-rtt-velocity.question: How much of a monkey's finger velocity does a fixed linear decoder recover from motor-cortex spiking, on held-out trials of the same session?
nlb-mc-rtt-velocity.label: Locally executed experiment · offline · one macaque, one session · not an official Neural Latents Benchmark score
nlb-mc-rtt-velocity.evidence: a locally executed experiment, not a score reported in a paper or on the benchmark leaderboard
nlb-mc-rtt-velocity.measured_quantity: spike counts of sorted units recorded by an electrode array in primary motor cortex; the decoded quantity is x/y finger velocity

design.split: the dataset's stored training and validation trials, interleaved within the one session; no random row split, and the test file was not opened
design.neurons: the held-in neurons only; the benchmark's held-out neurons are not inputs

signal.context: trailing spike-count history only, reset at every trial and observation gap
signal.target: the mean stored x/y finger velocity within a bin shifted by the target lag, in m/s

models.ridge: standardization fitted on the training rows, then ridge regression (alpha 10, Cholesky solver, with intercept); training-constant features dropped; no hyperparameter search
models.training_mean: predicts the training rows' mean velocity for every validation row

r2_uniform_average.name: R², uniform mean of x and y

comparison.note: The ridge improves R² and the root-mean-square error but has a larger mean absolute error than the training mean: it is not an unconditional winner, and both directions are shown.

uncertainty.reason: The validation rows are temporally correlated samples from one animal in one session, not independent subjects; no population interval is computed.

nlb-mc-rtt-velocity.reading: On held-out trials of the same session, the ridge recovers part of the variance of finger velocity where the training mean recovers none, and it lowers the root-mean-square error; its mean absolute error is higher than the training mean's.
limitations: One macaque and one recording session, with training and validation trials interleaved within it: no cross-day, cross-animal or human evidence. With one animal, every figure is that animal's.
A separate supervised diagnostic on the stored training and validation trials: not an official Neural Latents Benchmark score, not co-smoothing and not a latent-model comparison.

The velocity labels were derived offline from finger position, and the box average over each bin differs from the benchmark's own resampling, so equality with the benchmark's velocity score is not claimed.
Offline: not a real-time or closed-loop controller demonstration.
The validation rows are temporally correlated samples, not independent subjects.
claims_not_supported: not an official Neural Latents Benchmark score and not co-smoothing
no cross-day, cross-animal or human claim
no real-time or closed-loop control claim
the ridge is not better on every metric

independent_audit.checked: every feature and target row reconstructed independently of the code that produced it; the ridge coefficients checked against the normal equations; training-only normalization, prediction alignment and every metric recomputed
independent_audit.not_checked: the stored velocity itself, which the dataset derives offline from finger position

ds007420-optical-coverage.title: Human fNIRS recordings: are the optical values numerically usable?
ds007420-optical-coverage.question: Are the optical values of every recording finite and positive, with no exactly constant channel?
ds007420-optical-coverage.label: Locally executed check · label-independent · counts only
ds007420-optical-coverage.evidence: a locally executed check, not a score and not a result reported in a paper
ds007420-optical-coverage.measured_quantity: raw optical intensity at two wavelengths for each source–detector pair
ds007420-optical-coverage.definitions: Shares use every optical value as the denominator. A constant channel is one whose samples are all finite and exactly equal, with no tolerance.
ds007420-optical-coverage.reading: Every optical value of every recording is finite and positive, and no channel is exactly constant. That is basic numerical coverage, a precondition for further optical processing.
limitations: Coverage counts only: not signal-to-noise, scalp coupling, saturation, motion, wavelength-pair integrity, physiological plausibility, neural origin, task validity or decoding evidence. Positive, non-constant values alone cannot establish signal quality.
No classifier score exists. The numeric task codes have no verified lookup to hands or movements, and the event durations disagree between the events table, the optical files and the cited paper.
The auxiliary motion-sensor clocks are unverified and their holds stand: optical coverage does not repair them.
claims_not_supported: no signal quality, neural origin or activation claim

independent_audit.checked: every channel count reconciled against the recording totals and the aggregate; the code and its synthetic tests reviewed
independent_audit.not_checked: the raw-signal pass was not repeated

status_only.name: FALCON H2 · human intracortical handwriting
status_only.reason: Prepared, not scored: no model has been fitted. The label audit found every public minival trial inside the calibration data, so a leakage-safe diagnostic must first remove those trials from training.
facts: The public minival trials were inspected to find the overlap, so a later diagnostic on them would be exposed, not blinded, and would not be the official FALCON cross-day score.
The held-out calibration trials are inputs for few-shot recalibration, not independent evaluation data.
The cleaned training trials alone carry the symbol set; a CTC decoder adds one class for the blank.
